Treaties are interpreted under Articles 31–33 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties, which reflect customary international law. A treaty is read in good faith according to the ordinary meaning of its terms in their context and in light of its object and purpose, together with any subsequent agreement, subsequent practice, and relevant rules of international law. Preparatory work is only a supplementary means, used to confirm that reading or to resolve ambiguity, obscurity, or a manifestly absurd or unreasonable result.
CONFIDENCE: 92
